topic.title: Data Field Encapsulation
topic.description: Hiding data with getters and setters

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how to keep your code's data safe from accidental changes? Let's explore data field encapsulation!

• Why hiding data is a good thing
• How getters and setters work like bouncers
• How to protect your class's private parts (data!)

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine your class is a VIP nightclub. The data fields are the VIP guests inside. You wouldn't let just anyone walk in and mess with them, right?

That's where encapsulation comes in - it's like having bouncers (getters/setters) who control who gets access to what.

• **Private fields**: The VIP guests (data) that stay hidden
• **Public methods**: The bouncers (getters/setters) who control access
• **Validation**: The guest list that checks who's allowed in

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Encapsulation means making data fields private and providing public getter/setter methods
A getter (accessor) returns the value of a private field
A setter (mutator) sets the value of a private field with optional validation
Encapsulation protects data integrity by controlling how fields are accessed and modified
Convention: getFieldName() for getters, setFieldName(value) for setters

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Encapsulation hides data and exposes controlled access points. Always make fields private and add getters/setters as needed. Use setters to validate data before changing it. Practice by encapsulating real-world objects like bank accounts.
